<!-- tickmarkr:spec -->

Clicks, the wheel and hover act on the drawn surface wherever the terminal reports them — and every
pointer action has a key that does the same thing, proven by comparing drawn frames. THE PLAN STAYS
AUTHORITATIVE, now for input too: a click resolves to a target through planFrame's regions — the
same plan the conformance oracle pins — and a session resize is an INPUT the plan recomputes from,
never a bypass. The pointer layer never re-derives geometry; that defect was deleted in v1.83
(withBandGeometry) and does not return wearing a mouse.

## Authoring laws in force

Unchanged from v1.83: every `test:` criterion exists as a vitest test whose title matches the
criterion string verbatim, asserting on DRAWN frames and recorded state; no criterion satisfiable by
an absence, a rename, a source-text grep or an empty collection; every file below has exactly ONE
owning task, and tasks sharing a hub file are ORDERED; `npm test` stays zero-token; no new runtime
dependencies; no mark drawn anywhere; pointer enable sequences never reach run.ci or run.non-tty.

## Not in scope

Configuration surface (design contract first); host-terminal theme colours (design contract first,
seeded); compile-time vacuity checks (harness track — may run beside this bundle as a non-UI task
family if scoping wants both); persistence of any layout override; new keys beyond parity.

## T1: the pointer acts, and every hit resolves through the plan

- goal: clicks and the wheel act on the drawn run surface. HIT-TESTING LAW: a click maps to its target through planFrame's regions and rowSpans — the plan the conformance oracle pins — via one resolver in pointer.ts; no pointer path re-derives, rewrites or caches geometry the plan did not produce. THE SEAM FIX RIDES HERE: live.ts's key delivery defaults its column count (live.ts:254, the T14 reviewer's deferred finding), routing input as if the sidebar rail were always drawn; under pointers the target set depends on which bands the plan actually drew at the real width, so the seam requires the measured width and the default dies — the 64-to-79-column band is the proving ground. SGR-1006 reporting; wheel scrolls the panel under the pointer only; a click on a focusable panel moves the focus ring through the same transition its key uses. AMENDED after two review rounds (2026-07-31, .overseer/ORCH-ESCALATION-v184-T1-plan-authority-seam.md): the plan itself must PRODUCE the item-level geometry the pointer consumes — planFrame grows the item rows as FIRST-CLASS members of plan.regions and rowSpans — a parallel plan.items field the conformance oracle never pins is the dodge two review rounds already caught, and rail targets resolve from the plan's own rows, never from menuRows arithmetic; import PANEL_CHROME_ROWS from components.tsx rather than relocating it. The wheel NEVER retires another panel's filter prompt — wheeling over the rail leaves the body drawn as it was, proven with the prompt open. YOUR STARTING POINT: cherry-pick from preserve/v184-T1-four-rounds (d244c39f) — the SGR chunk-buffer, the click prompt-retire, and the wheel fix are done and reviewed; only the plan-authority geometry remains. A click while the filter prompt is open retires the prompt before dispatching the view transition — pointer input is never routed as a synthetic keystroke through whatever scope happens to be live

## T2: pointer hygiene — the terminal is borrowed, the keyboard is sovereign

- goal: pointer reporting is a loan the surface always repays: enabled only on an interactive terminal, disabled on every exit path including a thrown failure and a signal, and never emitted on the CI or non-tty surfaces, so the frozen machine anchors cannot carry an enable sequence by construction. The keyboard remains a complete interface: every pointer action has an advertised key producing the identical drawn frame, and pointer reports are a separate input class that no key handler ever receives

  - test: with no pointer reported the surface draws exactly what it draws with the pointer layer absent
  - test: every pointer action is performed by an advertised key as well, proven by driving both and comparing drawn frames
  - test: a pointer report changes no key handler state, while its paired key drives the same transition
  - judge: the terminal is left as it was found, and nothing in the surface is reachable only with a mouse

## T3: hover tells you what a click would hit

- goal: hovering highlights exactly the element the plan-resolver would return for a click at that cell — hover and click share one resolver, so the highlight cannot lie. Highlights are session-ephemeral drawn state: no highlight byte reaches any golden, anchor or colour capture, because captures record the pointerless appearance by construction. Highlight colour comes from the existing theme's semantic inks — no new colour, no theme change (the host-terminal-colour seed stays a separate design-contract decision)
- shape: implement

## T4: a panel resizes for this session, and the plan still owns every cell

- goal: dragging a panel boundary sets a session override that flows INTO planFrame as an input — the plan recomputes from the measured size plus the override, the renderer draws the recomputed plan unmodified, and the conformance oracle holds on every resized layout exactly as it holds on the default one. The override lives only in the running process: nothing is written anywhere, and a relaunch draws the default layout. A drag that would take a panel below its readable floor leaves it at the floor — elements surrender whole, per the contract, never collapse
- shape: implement
- deps: T3

- context: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-28-v1.83-watchsetup-contract.md, .overseer/AUDIT-v184-pointer-seed.md, src/tui/cockpit/live.ts

  - test: a resize never persists — relaunching draws the original layout
  - test: a drag below a panel's readable floor leaves it at the floor rather than collapsing it
  - test: the resized layout is planFrame's output and conformance holds on it, on launch and after further resizes
  - judge: a session override is an input to the plan, never a bypass of it — drawn still equals planned everywhere
